specName: 021 Generic Work Center — Optional Job Fill
expectations: the generic flow's steps, order and confirmation are unchanged when no job is running
the job is never the request's identity and never appears as a card cell
no new integration or endpoint is introduced
nothing about a declined offer is stored or shown again within the request
context: area: MTM_Waitlist.GenericRequest (step view models, draft, flow rules, live step data)
area: MTM_Waitlist.GenericRequest.Data (live part and die reads)
area: Database/StoredProcedures and Database/Tables (request persistence, provenance column)
constraint: every data operation goes through a stored procedure, with create.sql and rollback.sql beside it
constraint: internal stores are read and written live; external Visual reads go through the mock fallback shapes
constraint: no new integration; the job read reuses the work-order flow's own read (assumption A2)

FR-001.title: A running job at a generic work center is offered as a fill

FR-002.title: The choice is never made for the requester and the job is not read before it

FR-003.title: Declining leaves the flow unchanged, is not a failure, and is not asked again in that request

FR-004.title: No offer appears when no job is running

FR-005.title: Accepting pre-fills the answers the job carries

FR-006.title: Every pre-filled value says it came from the job

FR-007.title: Every pre-filled value stays changeable and a changed value is what the request carries

FR-008.title: A value the job does not carry is still asked of the requester
FR-008.assumes: A job that carries no part leaves the part step asking, which is the step's existing behaviour with an empty draft value.

FR-009.title: Changing the item clears the answers that belonged to the previous item

FR-010.title: A pre-filled value that its owning chunk proves is still proved

FR-011.title: A filled request keeps the generic identity and never takes the job as its identity

FR-012.title: A filled request draws the generic card with no work order cell

FR-013.title: The job is recorded and shown as provenance, distinct from identity

FR-014.title: A job that closes or changes before submission does not invalidate the request

FR-015.title: No offer is made to a person who may not see the job's data
FR-015.assumes: No permission in the application governs job visibility, so no requester is excluded and the gate point is named in one adapter.

FR-016.title: An unreadable job is reported unavailable with the attempt time and a retry

FR-017.title: Every remaining Temp artefact of this feature is deleted and the build stays green

intent: Let a generic work center offer to fill a request from the job running on it, with the job kept as provenance rather than identity.

decisions.decision: The offer is a panel on the Category step, probed when that step loads.
decisions.why: Launch from a work-center tile goes straight to Category, so the category step is the first step after the work center on both entry paths.
decisions.rejected: A new wizard step, or a ContentDialog raised from the work center view model.

decisions.decision: The fill seeds the job's part, sequence, die and dunnage and never the category or item.
decisions.why: The job carries no generic item code, and the item is the request's identity.
decisions.rejected: Mapping the job's part onto a generic item.

decisions.decision: Provenance is a new nullable provenance_work_order column.
decisions.why: active_setup_job_id means identity and is returned unconditionally by both request reads.
decisions.rejected: Reusing active_setup_job_id, or storing the job inside answers_json.

decisions.decision: The job read is an interface in the generic module, implemented at the composition root over IActiveJobItemResolverService.
decisions.why: No library in the solution references MTM_Waitlist.Setup, and RequestJobAvailabilityProvider already sets this pattern.
decisions.rejected: A project reference from the generic data library into Setup.

decisions.decision: The probe answers only the job's work order; values are read after acceptance.
decisions.why: FR-001 needs the job named, FR-002 forbids reading its values before the choice.
decisions.rejected: One read whose values are held back until accepted.

decisions.decision: A failed value read leaves the panel unavailable with the attempt time and a retry, and seeds nothing.
decisions.why: FR-016 asks for that report and forbids presenting a partly filled request as complete.
decisions.rejected: Failing the whole step, or silently continuing.

decisions.decision: The offer is not gated on a permission; the adapter carries a simplified note where a gate would go.
decisions.why: None of the twenty-one declared permissions governs seeing a job's data, and a new key would invent the role policy.
decisions.rejected: Gating on permission.setup.work_centers, or minting a new permission key.

decisions.decision: Provenance is rendered on the detail page only.
decisions.why: FR-012 forbids a job cell on the card and no request export exists.
decisions.rejected: A card cell, or inventing an export surface.

decisions.decision: The offer is answered by a per-request flag on the draft rather than by a step of its own.
decisions.why: The flow's step order is unchanged, and a declined offer must not be asked again within the request.
decisions.rejected: A new wizard step, or remembering the refusal anywhere outside the request.

decisions.decision: Each step seeds itself from the fill when it loads, not when the offer is accepted.
decisions.why: The category commit clears the answers below it, so a seed written at accept time would be wiped before the steps that use it ran.
decisions.rejected: Writing the seeded values into the draft at accept time.

decisions.decision: Changing the item drops the fill outright, work order included.
decisions.why: It is the clear rule the design already records: once the answers that belonged to the previous item are gone, no value in the request came from the job.
decisions.rejected: Keeping the work order and raising a request whose provenance names a job it draws nothing from.

decisions.decision: The detail page draws the provenance as the row label with the work order beside it.
decisions.why: Every row on that page is a label and a value, so the pinned sentence reads as the row rather than through a second surface.
decisions.rejected: A separate single-line block above the card.

decisions.decision: An item change only drops the fill when a different item was already chosen for this request.
decisions.why: The first item a request picks has nothing before it to carry anything over from, and clearing there threw the accepted fill away before any step could use it.
decisions.rejected: Clearing on every selection whose code differs from the stored one, which is every first selection.

decisions.decision: A category change drops the fill, but the first category picked does not.
decisions.why: The answers the fill supplied were statements about the item under the previous category; a request with no previous category has nothing to carry over.
decisions.rejected: Clearing unconditionally, which emptied the fill on the very pick that follows accepting it.

decisions.decision: A different work center drops the fill and reopens the offer.
decisions.why: The question that was answered was about the other work center's job, so the new work center's own job must be offered (FR-001, FR-003).
decisions.rejected: Keeping the fill and the answered flag, which showed a job at a press the request had left.

decisions.decision: The job's die and part are candidates held outside the draft until their own reads return them.
decisions.why: A seeded die or part that the source does not record must not be raised, and the fill must never stand in for the read that proves it (FR-010, 020 FR-002).
decisions.rejected: Writing the values into the draft at load time, which left an unproved part or die on a request when the read found nothing.

specify.summary: Planned an optional job fill asked on the Category step, seeded onto the part, dunnage and die steps, with provenance stored on the request.
specify.key_finding: The work center step is skipped on the normal launch path, so the offer belongs on the Category step.

tasks.summary: 31 tasks: foundational schema, seam and write path, then User Story 1 (offer and seeding), User Story 2 (provenance), then polish.

implement.summary: The generic flow now offers to fill a request from the job running at the work center, seeds the job's part, die and dunnage as changeable candidates, and records the job as provenance on the raised request.

approach: A new job-fill seam in the generic module, implemented at the composition root over the Setup module's existing active-job read, drives a panel on the Category step. Accepting seeds the job's part, sequence, die and dunnage onto the draft as changeable candidates, and the job is written to a new provenance column through the existing request write path.

concerns.note: simplified: the offer is not gated on a permission, because the application declares none that governs seeing a job's data. When one is added it belongs in GenericRequestJobFillSource, before the read. FR-015's condition therefore cannot arise today.
The stored-procedure changes are authored and mirrored but were not applied to a live database in this run: the schema and procedure integration tests are among the environment-gated skips.

The first independent review found a defect that made the feature inert: the accepted fill was discarded on the first item pick because the draft had no previous item code. Fixed, with a regression test covering the first pick and a changed one.

last_action: Build and full suite green after the offer, the seeds and the provenance landed.
